tldr: Sustained-policy comparisons can remain scarce even as a switchback experiment records more outcomes. For fair independent assignments, public exact memory \(L\), and unrestricted bounded fixed schedules, the critical scale is \(\lambda_T=T2^{-L}\). We derive the scalar Poisson-binomial critical experiment and its explicit squared-risk profile, certify the connected-interval value by finite rational primal-dual games, construct original-record attainers with exact finite-design coverage, and prove matching converses against every full-record procedure. A labelled-run comparison and a legal block-correlated prior transfer the scalar values uniformly to the causal schedule class. The result gives a computable precision benchmark for sustained marketplace policy evaluation under the stated public-memory model.
gap: The checked switchback testing and design-based minimax sources do not give sharp critical precision against all procedures using the complete record, jointly for point estimation and honest connected intervals.
